repaired_row_as_shipped.boundary_rationale: This row closes the cosmos catalog across two interior turns. הַֽ֭תְקַשֵּׁר מַעֲדַנּ֣וֹת כִּימָ֑ה, “Can you bind the cluster of the Pleiades, or loosen the cords of Orion?” (web:Job.38.31), opens the constellations item on a patah-plus-meteg interrogative-he (not the more common hataf-patah spelling; the same patah-plus-meteg spelling recurs only at its sibling verse inside this row, 38:35 — sweep: 2 within the 38:16-39:12 catalog window; book-wide the spelling occurs in 9 verses (8 interrogative)), running through the heavens' laws at verse 33 (“Do you know the laws of the heavens? Can you establish its dominion over the earth?”, web:Job.38.33). הֲתָרִ֣ים לָעָ֣ב קוֹלֶ֑ךָ, “Can you lift up your voice to the clouds, that abundance of waters may cover you?” (web:Job.38.34) turns to weather and, at verse 36, to a bare מִי שָׁ֭ת בַּטֻּח֣וֹת חָכְמָ֑ה, “Who has put wisdom in the inward parts? Or who has given understanding to the mind?” (web:Job.38.36) — the catalog's turn toward wisdom, a two-verse pair rather than one event: מִֽי יְסַפֵּ֣ר שְׁחָקִ֣ים בְּחָכְמָ֑ה, “Who can count the clouds by wisdom?” (web:Job.38.37), repeats the same bare-מי wisdom opener immediately after. The whole cosmos catalog then closes on the mundane image of dust caking into clods (“when the dust runs into a mass, and the clods of earth stick together?”, web:Job.38.38), before verse 39 opens the animal catalog with a fresh interrogative aimed at the lioness. The he-interrogative opener recurring across this whole span is texture, not the discriminator by itself: fifteen verses open on it between 38:16 and 39:12, of which five run consecutively inside this row alone (31-35); this row's own edges rest instead on the topic shifts named above — constellations, weather, wisdom, dust.
repaired_row_as_shipped.strongest_rejected_alternative: Ending the cosmos catalog at verse 33 with the constellations, so that 34-38's weather-and-wisdom material would open a fresh row, was considered. No speech or scene marker separates 38:33 from 38:34 — but by that same test no speech or scene marker separates 38:30 from 38:31 or 38:38 from 38:39 either, so the criterion cannot be what distinguishes this row's own edges from the rejected seam; the ground here is instead the topic continuity of 31-38 as one movement through the sky's phenomena, closing on dust before the animal catalog's fresh subject at 39.
repaired_row_as_shipped.literature_type_guess: Constellations and heaven's laws turning through weather to inward wisdom, closing on dust and clods

neighbour_prev_post_repair.boundary_rationale: The precipitation cluster opens on the same one-word interrogative opener that opened the row above, הֲ֭בָאתָ (sweep: 2 verses book-wide, Job.38.16 and Job.38.22 only; the clause diverges immediately after), continuing אֶל אֹצְר֣וֹת שָׁ֑לֶג, “Have you entered the storehouses of the snow, or have you seen the storehouses of the hail,” (web:Job.38.22). Interior turns follow at every new form water takes: אֵי זֶ֣ה הַ֭דֶּרֶךְ יֵחָ֣לֶק, “By what way is the lightning distributed, or the east wind scattered on the earth?” (web:Job.38.24) — the same interrogative-adverb-plus-demonstrative device that stands at 38:19, inside the preceding unit (38:16-38:21) rather than at its edge (sweep: 2 book-wide, its only two members), recurring here mid-cluster rather than at an edge, disclosed rather than denied; its own two subjects, light and the east wind, are an outlier inside this otherwise water-forms cluster, not a further form of water. מִֽי פִלַּ֣ג לַשֶּׁ֣טֶף תְּעָלָ֑ה, “Who has cut a channel for the flood water, or the path for the thunderstorm,” (web:Job.38.25) turns to the flood channel on a fresh verse-initial bare מי, a member the interior-turn list must include alongside הֲיֵשׁ לַמָּטָ֥ר אָ֑ב, “Does the rain have a father? Who has given birth to the gray frost of the sky?” (web:Job.38.29), where the same pronoun sits as the verse's second word rather than its opener. neighbour_prev_post_repair.strongest_rejected_alternative: Breaking this cluster at 27|28 into storehouses-and-channels versus parentage-and-birth was considered and set aside on the ice/frost thematic close that unifies 22-30, but the live rival is the seam at 38:23|38:24: snow and hail reserved for a day of battle, “which I have reserved against the time of trouble, against the day of battle and war?” (web:Job.38.23), against the turn to the way of light and the east wind at 38:24. The OSHB extract carries a ketiv/qere pair inside this formula (ketiv מנ against qere מִ֥ן, both shown adjacent above), the same pairing that opens 38:1 but here WITHOUT the definite article that 38:1 carries on the noun for whirlwind — a spelling difference between the two YHWH-speech openers, disclosed here rather than assumed. The speech immediately re-issues the gird-up command that opened the earlier whirlwind speech, oshb:Job.40.7 “אֱזָר נָ֣א כְגֶ֣בֶר חֲלָצֶ֑יךָ אֶ֝שְׁאָלְךָ֗ וְהוֹדִיעֵֽנִי”, web:Job.40.7 “Now brace yourself like a man. I will question you, and you will answer me.”; the two-word core כגבר חלציך is a genuine repeated device (sweep: 2 book-wide, skeleton: 38:3 and 40:7 only), binding the two whirlwind speeches as parallel re-openings. The strophe develops the challenge through two rhetorical questions closing at web:Job.40.9 “Or do you have an arm like God? Can you thunder with a voice like him?” (the second bearing a paseq, single-witness), before an imperative series reopens the address at 40:10.

neighbour_next_post_repair.boundary_rationale: The Behemoth poem opens on the full creature-introduction phrase, oshb:Job.40.15 “הִנֵּה נָ֣א בְ֭הֵמוֹת אֲשֶׁר עָשִׂ֣יתִי עִמָּ֑ךְ חָ֝צִ֗יר כַּבָּקָ֥ר יֹאכֵֽל”, web:Job.40.15 “See now behemoth, which I made as well as you. He eats grass as an ox.” — the presentative הִנֵּה נָ֣א plus the named creature בְ֭הֵמוֹת plus the אֲשֶׁר-relative clause together, not the bare presentative particle alone: הִנֵּה נָ֣א itself recurs verse-initially inside this row's own span, at 40:16 (הִנֵּה נָ֣א כֹח֣וֹ בְמָתְנָ֑יו וְ֝אֹנ֗וֹ בִּשְׁרִירֵ֥י בִטְנֽוֹ, “Look now, his strength is in his thighs. His force is in the muscles of his belly.”), and a third presentative-class opening, the hen variant without נא, sits at 40:23 (הֵ֤ן יַעֲשֹׁ֣ק נָ֭הָר לֹ֣א יַחְפּ֑וֹז יִבְטַ֓ח כִּֽי יָגִ֖יחַ יַרְדֵּ֣ן אֶל פִּֽיהוּ) — both disclosed here rather than passed over, since the bare particle class does not by itself uniquely locate 40:15; the fuller phrase quoted above, with its named creature and relative clause, has no counterpart at either recurrence. בהמות here names the creature, distinct from the same consonant string's common-plural sense (beasts/animals) at oshb:Job.12.7 “וְֽאוּלָ֗ם שְׁאַל נָ֣א בְהֵמ֣וֹת וְתֹרֶ֑ךָּ וְע֥וֹף הַ֝שָּׁמַ֗יִם וְיַגֶּד לָֽךְ”, web:Job.12.7 “But ask the animals now, and they will teach you; the birds of the sky, and they will tell you.” — a genuine homograph hazard, independently re-derived here: the bare (unprefixed) noun sweeps to 2 book-wide members (12:7 the common plural, 40:15 the creature), a distinct object from the prefixed מבהמות at 35:11, outside this bare count. The poem runs through body description to its theological center, web:Job.40.19 “He is the chief of the ways of God. He who made him gives him his sword.”, then habitat and security, closing on a capture-challenge question, web:Job.40.24 “Shall any take him when he is on the watch, or pierce through his nose with a snare?”, that sets up the Leviathan capture-challenge opening the next row. No interrogative, vocative, or formula interrupts between 40:15 and 40:24; the poem runs as one continuous description, at the wide end of the strophe guide but not beyond it.
